gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns applying a pointwise generator gradient identity to every observable in the orbit-limit domain, including nonsmooth observables. ISSUE-002 concerns transferring norm-based generator and Taylor arguments from strongly continuous to bi-continuous semigroups; it does not identify the missing differentiability/core restriction for the gradient formula.

The gold defect is the missing identification and continuity justification in the Lie-Trotter norm-convergence derivation, including the relation between bi-continuous and norm generators. ISSUE-002 instead challenges an asserted unchanged extension of a higher-order Hansen-Ostermann proof to bi-continuous semigroups and does not diagnose the specific Lie-Trotter factor-continuity and integrated-generator argument.

The gold issue is the unsupported global first-order rate due to missing local O(h^2) defect and domain regularity. ISSUE-001 identifies a separate Taylor-expression typo involving V(0)^{p+1} versus a time derivative; it does not recognize the missing quantitative local-defect estimate needed for the rate.

The gold issue requires the Strang-specific O(h^3) local defect, symmetry cancellation, and corresponding domain bounds for an O(n^{-2}) rate. ISSUE-002 discusses whether norm-based higher-order arguments transfer to the bi-continuous setting, but does not diagnose the missing Strang local estimate or regularity assumptions.

The gold defect is the absence of analytic-sector hypotheses ensuring that complex-time semigroup factors are defined. ISSUE-003 corrects an algebraic formula for the composition parameter a_k; it does not address existence of the complex-time factors or analytic extensions.

The gold issue is the unjustified removal of the leading V_p power and the resulting need for uniform power stability in the telescoping estimate. ISSUE-002 concerns norm-versus-tau generator arguments and proof transfer, not stability bounds for powers of the composed approximation.

The gold issue is that full-flow invariance does not imply that each frozen coordinate subflow preserves Omega, so the coordinate operators may be undefined. ISSUE-007 identifies incorrect frozen-variable subscripts in two algorithmic calls; correcting those calls does not establish the missing frozen-flow invariance or global-existence hypothesis.

The gold issue concerns evaluating a third-order routine at nonreal times under only a real-flow contract, requiring complex-time extensions and a complexified state domain. ISSUE-003 concerns an incorrect algebraic formula for splitting coefficients, not the well-definedness of complex-time flow evaluations.
